meeting_header:
Date: 2029-08-23 14:30 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Mark (AE), Priya (SE), Sam (Solutions) - Redwood; Jonas (CTO), Lina (Head, Cloud Partnerships), Ravi (SRE), Sophie (Biz Ops) - AstraCompute
Recording: Enabled
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood Inference and AstraCompute to explore a hybrid GPU onramp/channel integration. Topics covered: deployment models (hosted, dedicated, private/VPC), kernel and driver compatibility for Astra's GPU fleet, quantization and batching tradeoffs, security/compliance (SOC2/KMS/SSO), revenue/share/pricing sketch for channel partnership. Agreed next steps include sharing architecture deck, security checklist, and running a short compatibility lab between SE teams.
topics: partner intro; hybrid onramp architecture; GPU SKUs and drivers; quantization & inference performance; private/VPC deployment and air-gap options; SSO/KMS/compliance; pricing and channel economics; pilot success criteria
transcript:
[00:00] Mark (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Uh, I think we've got about, what, 50-odd minutes today. So we'll run through quick intros and then dig into how Redwood could hook into Astra's hybrid GPU onramp offering.
[00:15] Jonas (CTO): Yep, sounds great. Appreciate you making time. I'm Jonas, CTO. Lina's on for partnerships, Ravi from SRE, and Sophie handling ops.
[00:28] Priya (SE): Hi, Priya here, I'm the Redwood solutions engineer, focusing on private deployments and kernel compatibility testing. Sam from solutions is here as well.
[00:38] Sophie (Biz Ops): Morning, thanks. Quick ask — can we get the ROI sketch? Our finance team will want rough numbers early.
[00:45] Mark (AE): Absolutely, we'll include a rough pricing sketch. We'll flag reserved capacity pricing and channel discounts.
[00:53] Lina (Partnerships): High level, AstraCompute runs a mix of on-prem racks for enterprise customers and a multi-tenant cloud offering. We're exploring beefing up a partner onramp so customers can seamlessly burst between Astra cloud and our co-located partners.
[01:10] Priya (SE): Nice. When you say racks, are we talking DGX-class nodes or — like which GPUs?
[01:18] Ravi (SRE): Mostly custom OAM boards with Ampere A120-ish and older A100 fleet, a few Hopper prototypes. Drivers are R525-ish, kernel 5.15.
[01:28] Priya (SE): Okay that's helpful. Redwood's runtime has specific kernel/driver heuristics — we pre-select execution kernels based on model arch and sequence length. So driver mismatch can surface as perf cliffs if quant kernels don't line up.
[01:40] Jonas (CTO): Right, and we want to avoid any long integration windows. What's a typical discovery-to-pilot timeline?
[01:47] Mark (AE): From past partners, for a quick compatibility lab plus a pilot, around 3–6 weeks. The lab is basically 2–4 hours where SEs run a couple of models and kernel traces.
[01:57] Priya (SE): Yeah the quick-lab we propose is two parts: 1) kernel/driver sanity and 2) inference workflow with quantized artifacts. We'll test a standard Llama-variant and a transformer encoder-decoder sample.
[02:12] Ravi (SRE): How invasive is that? We can't touch customers' prod networks — everything needs to run in our staging VPC.
[02:19] Priya (SE): No problem. We can run inside your staging VPC or provide a small infra repo that spins an isolated test harness. We can also do air-gapped runs if needed, though that's slightly more involved.
[02:31] Lina (Partnerships): Good to hear. On the commercial side, curious how Redwood structures channel deals — do you allow reseller margins, co-sell credits?
[02:40] Mark (AE): Yes. We support channel resellers and offer partner discounts for committed capacity. Typically there's a revenue share on reserved capacity and a rebate for partner-led signups. We'll share a one-pager.
[02:50] Sophie (Biz Ops): For procurement, we also need to know compliance posture — SOC2, ISO, KMS support, audit logs.
[02:58] Sam (Solutions): Redwood is SOC2-certified, we support KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM integrations via PKCS11). We also provide audit logs and token-level tracing in the console. I'll attach the security checklist.
[03:12] Jonas (CTO): Great. On tech, two specific concerns: 1) quantization — we have customers that need INT8 for cost reasons, 2) KV cache sharing for chat workloads across bursts.
[03:23] Priya (SE): For INT8, we have quantization profiles per architecture and per model family; some of them require particular math libraries or CUDA kernels. For KV cache, our runtime preserves and can persist prefix caches at route level, but cross-node cache replication depends on the deployment mode — for Dedicated we have faster KV persistence integrated with Redis or local NVMe-backed stores.
[03:41] Ravi (SRE): If we run Redwood private in our VPC, what does networking look like? Do you need a control plane connection out to Redwood?
[03:49] Priya (SE): For Redwood Private we offer a customer-managed control plane option — the control plane can run in your VPC or we can offer an on-prem bundle. There's an optional outbound control channel for telemetry; it's not required for core inference if you want fully air-gapped.
[04:05] Jonas (CTO): Can we get details on the on-prem bundle? Our regulated customers prefer an air-gap but want managed updates.
[04:12] Mark (AE): We'll include the on-prem package doc. High-level, updates are either shipped as signed artifacts you pull, or via a managed connector that you approve.
[04:21] Lina (Partnerships): On the partner integration pattern — what parts of Redwood are exposed to our customers? Is it just an API endpoint and model catalog, or do we white-label?
[04:30] Sam (Solutions): You can embed via API or host a localized model catalog. We also support route-level branding tokens and per-tenant RBAC. Full white-label may need some legal work, but engineers can route customers to your branded endpoint via reverse proxy.
[04:45] Sophie (Biz Ops): On pricing again, banding for reserved capacity — do you provide burst slots?
[04:50] Mark (AE): Yes, reserved with burst. We generally commit base capacity and allow bursts billed at a higher per-token rate. For channel partners, we can carve out a pool that you resell.
[04:59] Jonas (CTO): One thing — we run a very spiky workload, so batching is tricky. Does Redwood do continuous batching without adding tail latency?
[05:08] Priya (SE): Our runtime uses workload-aware batching and latency SLOs. You can set per-route SLOs and the router will prefer lower-latency paths for routes that need it. There's also adaptive batching so bursty traffic isn't penalized.
[05:22] Ravi (SRE): Are there logs or traces we can plug into our observability stack? We use Grafana and Jaeger.
[05:28] Sam (Solutions): Yes — we expose Prometheus metrics, OpenTelemetry traces, and per-request trace IDs you can correlate with Jaeger/Grafana.
[05:36] Jonas (CTO): Good. Can you run a demo of the quick-lab — like sample LLM perf in our staging?
[05:42] Priya (SE): We usually schedule a two-hour kernel lab. We'll need a small compute slice and SSH to an orchestrator -- or we can run inside your tenant in the cloud. The goal is to validate quant kernels and confirm no perf cliffs.
[05:55] Lina (Partnerships): From a go-to-market perspective, what artifacts do you give partners? Co-marketing pack? Sales enablement?
[06:02] Mark (AE): Yes — partner playbook, quickstart templates, co-branded decks, and a partners portal. We'll share a sample partner playbook.
[06:10] Sophie (Biz Ops): For legal — do you require exclusivity? Some of our vendors ask for regional exclusivity.
[06:16] Mark (AE): No standard exclusivity; we handle custom channel agreements on a case-by-case basis. Typically we avoid exclusive long-term clauses unless there's mutual business justification.
[06:27] Jonas (CTO): On measuring pilot success — what are typical metrics? Throughput? P99 latency? Cost per 1k tokens?
[06:34] Priya (SE): All of the above. For pilot we propose: p50/p95/p99 latency targets, cost per 1k tokens aligned to a baseline model, and correctness/regression checks on a shared prompt set. We can run model A/B comparisons.
[06:48] Ravi (SRE): For the prompt sets — we'll need to keep customer data out of shared samples. Any guidance?
[06:54] Sam (Solutions): We recommend synthetic prompt sets or anonymized samples. We have a prompt masking tool and you can also use local eval harnesses if you prefer not to send any real data off your network.
[07:06] Jonas (CTO): Okay — two technical nitty-gritty points before we wrap: 1) Do you support custom kernels for our Hopper prototypes? 2) Any special NVLink requirements?
[07:18] Priya (SE): 1) We can incorporate custom kernels but it requires a short validation cycle; our platform supports plugin kernels. 2) NVLink is supported for local multi-GPU execution; however, across nodes we rely on our KV cache strategies rather than NVLink. We'll need to map your topology to our runtime to recommend best layout.
[07:36] Lina (Partnerships): I heard you mention Smart routing earlier, can you summarize that?
[07:42] Sam (Solutions): Smart routing allows rules to route requests by latency targets, cost tiers, or model family. Example: VIP customers go to lower-latency Dedicated pool; cost-sensitive jobs go to cheaper quantized variants. This is where partner pools can be prioritized.
[07:58] Sophie (Biz Ops): About audit logs — does Redwood keep token-level traces forever by default? We need retention policies.
[08:05] Mark (AE): No, retention is configurable. Default is 90 days for detailed traces, but you can extend or shorten per contract. We also support customer-managed retention via Private deployments.
[08:16] Jonas (CTO): Great. Can you share a sample architecture diagram?
[08:20] Priya (SE): We'll send a deck with diagrams showing hosted flow, dedicated pool, private VPC, and on-prem air-gap variants. We'll annotate where KV caches and batchers live.
[08:31] (crosstalk)
[08:35] Mark (AE): Quick recap then — we'll share: 1) partner one-pager and playbook, 2) security/compliance checklist and SOC2 artifacts, 3) an architecture deck, 4) propose times for the 2-hr compatibility lab.
[08:47] Lina (Partnerships): Sounds good. Any rough pricing numbers now?
[08:51] Mark (AE): Ballpark — hosted pay-as-you-go ranges, but for reserved channel pools, think in terms of committed monthly GPU-hours + a per-token operational fee. We'll send a sketch, not a final quote.
[09:02] Jonas (CTO): For the lab, what sample models would be best? We run general LLM chat and a vector-embedding pipeline for similarity search.
[09:09] Priya (SE): We'll pick a small chat model (Llama-variant) and a transformer encoder for embeddings. We'll also test batching and KV cache persistence across bursts.
[09:19] Ravi (SRE): If the kernel lab succeeds, what does onboarding look like? How many people do we need on our side?
[09:25] Sam (Solutions): Typically 2 infra folks and 1 engineering contact for the pilot. Redwood SEs will run the tests and work with your SREs. Pilot onboarding usually takes 2–3 weeks and then a production ramp.
[09:39] Sophie (Biz Ops): Can you include an example SLA for Dedicated? Our customers will ask for 99.9 up-time.
[09:45] Mark (AE): Yes, our Dedicated SLA options include 99.9 and 99.95 with scaling and support tiers. We'll attach sample SLA language.
[09:53] Jonas (CTO): On the integration side, we'd like to automate customer provisioning — can Redwood integrate with our tenant onboarding flow?
[09:59] Priya (SE): Yes — we have APIs and Terraform modules for provisioning routes, models, and RBAC. We'll share example Terraform modules.
[10:09] Lina (Partnerships): What's your typical legal/contract cadence for partner pilots? 30 days? 90?
[10:15] Mark (AE): Short pilots can be 30 days with limited capacity. For full pilots we suggest 90 days to capture different load patterns. Legal templates are partner-friendly and we'll propose standard MSA/partner addendum.
[10:26] Jonas (CTO): Any red flags we should be aware of moving forward?
[10:29] Priya (SE): Mostly driver/kernel mismatches — but we can usually resolve that in the lab. Also quantization edge-cases for some models — we flag those during tests.
[10:38] Ravi (SRE): Last question — can you provide a contact for escalation during pilot?
[10:41] Mark (AE): Yep, I'll be the commercial lead, Priya the technical lead, and Sam will be primary solutions contact. We'll add a 24/7 escalation channel if we set a Dedicated SLA.
[10:51] (brief pause)
[10:55] Mark (AE): Alright, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts and propose lab times.
[11:01] Lina (Partnerships): Thanks, looking forward to it.
[11:05] Jonas (CTO): Thanks all.
[11:08] (meeting ends)

Notes: transcript contains some speaker overlaps and occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., kernel numbers approximated). Attachments discussed: partner-playbook.pdf (link shared in chat), security-checklist.xlsx (link), architecture-deck.gdoc (link).
